1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	Add the `error` edge above **only when the requirements say what should happen if the call fails.** With no error edge, a failed call faults the flow — the correct, visible default.
176	
177	When an HTTP node does have an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly. Never set the flag on an HTTP node with no error edge — it suppresses the fault, so a failed call flows on and the run reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
178	
179	```json
180	{
181	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
182	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
183	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
184	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
185	  "targetPort": "input"
186	}
187	```
188	
189	### Debug
190	
191	| Error | Cause | Fix |
192	| --- | --- | --- |
193	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
194	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
195	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
196	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
197	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |

1	# HTTP Request Node — Planning
2	
3	> **MUST READ FIRST — confirm Managed HTTP Request fits your use case before authoring:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md). This planning doc is the flow-specific layer on top of it.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests — both connector-authenticated and manual. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated and does not pass IS credentials at runtime.
10	
11	## When to Use a Managed HTTP Request Node
12	
13	| Situation | Use Managed HTTP? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Connector exists but lacks the specific curated activity | Yes — connector mode ([impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md)), **if the connector supports HTTP request activity** (verify `HasHttpRequest` — see [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)) |
16	| No connector exists, but service has a REST API | Yes — manual mode ([impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md)) |
17	| Quick prototyping against any REST API | Yes — manual mode ([impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md)) |
18	| Connector exists and covers the use case | No — use [Connector Activity](../connector/planning.md) |
19	| Target system has no API (desktop app) | No — use [RPA Workflow](../rpa/planning.md) |
20	
21	For the two-mode concept (connector vs. manual) and the `url` / auth rules per mode, see the platform doc linked at the top.
22	
23	## Ports
24	
25	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| `input` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic, one per `inputs.branches` entry) |
28	
29	- `default` — primary success output, or fallback when configured branches don't match.
30	- `error` — implicit error port; fires when the call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Shared with all action nodes — see [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
31	- `branch-{id}` — HTTP-specific, configured via `inputs.branches` (response-content routing). See [Conditional Branches](#conditional-branches) below.
32	
33	## Output Variables
34	
35	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — `{ body, code, method, rawStringBody, request }` on success
36	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — `{ code, message, detail, category, status }` when the error port fires
37	
38	## Conditional Branches
39	
40	Use `inputs.branches` when you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., empty vs non-empty results). For generic call-failure handling, prefer the shared `error` port instead — don't enumerate every bad status code as a branch.
41	
42	Each branch's `conditionExpression` is a JS expression with `$self` bound to the current HTTP node's output:
43	
44	```json
45	{
46	  "inputs": {
47	    "branches": [
48	      { "id": "hasItems",  "name": "Has Items",  "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
49	      { "id": "empty",     "name": "Empty",      "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
50	    ]
51	  }
52	}
53	```
54	
55	Wire `branch-hasItems` / `branch-empty` as source ports on outgoing edges. `default` fires when no branch condition matches.
56	
57	> **Do not use `=js:` on `conditionExpression`** — HTTP branch conditions are evaluated as JS automatically (same rule as decision/switch expressions). See [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#http-branch-condition-inputsbranchesconditionexpression).
58	
59	## Dynamic values
60	
61	IS activity input fields (`url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` under `bodyParameters`) do **not** resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — the template runner only applies to native flow fields. Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value; template literals with `${...}` interpolation or string concatenation both work. See [Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query) for the full rationale and examples.
62	
63	## Key Inputs (`--detail` for `node configure`)
64	
65	Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with a `--detail` JSON. The CLI builds the full `inputs.detail` payload, `bindings_v2.json`, and connection resource files automatically. **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`.**
66	
67	**Connector mode** (IS connection auth):
68	
69	| `--detail` Key | Required | Description |
70	| --- | --- | --- |
71	| `authentication` | Yes | `"connector"` |
72	| `method` | Yes | HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE |
73	| `targetConnector` | Yes | Target connector key (e.g., `"uipath-salesforce-slack"`) |
74	| `connectionId` | Yes | Target connector's IS connection ID (from `uip is connections list --all-folders`) |
75	| `folderKey` | Yes | Orchestrator folder key (from `uip is connections list --all-folders`) |
76	| `url` | No | API endpoint URL/path (e.g., `"/conversations.replies"`). Auto-fills both `bodyParameters.path` and `bodyParameters.url`. |
77	| `query` | No | Query parameters as key-value object |
78	| `headers` | No | Additional headers as key-value object |
79	| `body` | No | Request body (for POST/PUT/PATCH). Connector mode is **`application/json` only** (request and response) — no other content type. |
80	
81	**Manual mode** (no connector auth):
82	
83	| `--detail` Key | Required | Description |
84	| --- | --- | --- |
85	| `authentication` | Yes | `"manual"` |
86	| `method` | Yes | HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE |
87	| `url` | Yes | Full target URL |
88	| `query` | No | Query parameters as key-value object |
89	| `headers` | No | Additional headers as key-value object |
90	| `body` | No | Request body (for POST/PUT/PATCH) |
91	
92	## Prerequisites
93	
94	- `uip login` required (for both modes — node type comes from registry)
95	- For connector mode: connector must support the HTTP request activity — verify the `HasHttpRequest` flag via `uip is connectors get "<connector-key>"`. If false, fall back to manual mode — confirm the switch with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
96	- For connector mode: a healthy IS connection must exist for the **target connector**. If none exists, auto-fall-through to manual mode is the recommended fallback — but confirm the mode switch with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md Step 2 — HTTP-specific recovery](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection) for the user-confirmation flow (switch-to-manual / create-now / skip).
97	- `uip maestro flow registry pull` to cache the `core.action.http.v2` definition
98	
99	## Planning Annotation
100	
101	In the architectural plan, annotate managed HTTP nodes as:
102	- Connector mode: `managed-http: <service> — <operation>` (e.g., "managed-http: Slack — GET /conversations.replies")
103	- Manual mode: `managed-http: manual — <method> <url>` (e.g., "managed-http: manual — GET https://api.example.com/data")
104

2	
3	Use this walkthrough when the target service has an IS connector and you want managed auth (OAuth / API key) handled by an existing IS connection.
4	
5	**Prerequisite:** a healthy IS connection for the target connector. Step 2 verifies this. If none exists, propose manual mode as the fallback and confirm the switch with the user before finalizing — do not switch modes without that confirmation.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–5 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	> **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` to set `parentId`. Without it, the node runs outside the loop context and outputs are null. See [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
17	
18	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Steps 2 and 3 reuse it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 3 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
19	
20	## Step 2 — Identify target connection
21	
22	**Connector mode only works if the connector supports the HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<target-connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag. If the flag is false, **STOP** — a connection cannot help. Use the recovery question below (switch to manual mode / skip / something else; the create-a-connection option does not apply) and do not switch modes without confirmation.
23	
24	```bash
25	uip is connections list "<target-connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
26	```
27	
28	`--all-folders` is mandatory for discovery. Selection rules, empty-result recovery, and ping verification live in the platform skill — do not duplicate them here.
29	
30	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md).
31	
32	Record the chosen connection's `Id` and `FolderKey` — Step 3 needs both.
33	
34	> **HTTP-specific recovery — no usable connection.** If platform-skill recovery yields nothing (empty after `--all-folders` + `--refresh`, user declines to create one), the HTTP node has unique fallback options. Ask the user to confirm the path — **manual mode is the recommended auto-fallback**, pre-selected, since it unblocks the node without a connection:
35	>
36	> - **Switch this node to manual mode** *(recommended)* — abandon this walkthrough and follow [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md). Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so this needs explicit confirmation.
37	> - **Create a new connection now** — `uip is connections create "<target-connector-key>"` starts the OAuth flow. User completes browser auth themselves, then re-run `uip is connections list` to pick up the new connection.
38	> - **Skip this node**.
39	> - **Something else**.
40	>
41	> Auto-try the fallback, but do not finalize a mode switch without the user's confirmation; do not invent a placeholder ID; do not skip the node without explicit selection. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
42	
43	## Step 3 — Configure the node
44	
45	> **STOP — open the platform skill before configuring.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, read [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md) and resolve every value you don't already have (IDs from names, required body fields, endpoint path, response shape).
46	>
47	> - **If the target connector is listed in that skill's `vendor-docs-registry.json`:** you MUST follow its **Step 0 (Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs)** — read the `docsUrl` + `notes` and confirm the exact endpoint with the `http-request` probe before running `node configure`. Pass the endpoint path verbatim: vendor method names can contain literal dots (Slack ``chat.postMessage`) — the dot is part of the path segment.
48	> - **If the connector is NOT listed:** the registry-grounding step does not apply — resolve missing values via the `http-request` probe / vendor docs as usual.
49	
50	```bash
51	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
52	  --detail '{
53	    "authentication": "connector",
54	    "targetConnector": "<target-connector-key>",
55	    "connectionId": "<target-connection-id>",
56	    "folderKey": "<folder-key>",
57	    "method": "GET",
58	    "url": "/api/endpoint",
59	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
60	  }' --output json
61	```
62	
63	> **Connector mode supports `application/json` request and response bodies only.**
64	
65	The CLI:
66	
67	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (connector, connectionId, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
68	- Auto-fills both `bodyParameters.path` and `bodyParameters.url` from the single `url` value you pass
69	- Generates `bindings_v2.json`

75	
76	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 5 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).

78	## Step 5 — Wire edges
79	
80	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 4 entry). Wire `default` to the next node.
